additions.reason: The supreme, hidden glory that transcends the ten utterances and sustains even the fallen places. The dominant concept of Package 1.
additions.source_quote: כִּי 'אַיֵּה' מְקוֹם כְּבוֹדוֹ – זֶה בְּחִינַת הַכָּבוֹד עֶלְיוֹן שֶׁל הַמַּאֲמָר הָעֶלְיוֹן, דְּהַיְנוּ הַמַּאֲמָר סָתוּם בְּרֵאשִׁית

additions.reason: The sealed/hidden utterance (Bereshit) that encompasses all ten utterances and from which even the fallen places receive life. Explicitly equated with 'אַיֵּה' and with the supreme kavod.
additions.source_quote: כִּי אַיֵּה הוּא בְּחִינוֹת מַאֲמָר סָתוּם, שֶׁהֵם מְקַבְּלִין חִיּוּת מִשָּׁם

additions.reason: The word/cry 'Ayeh' (where?) is identified as a bechina of the maamar satum and the supreme kavod. When one calls out 'where is His glory?' one is already connected to the hidden glory itself.
additions.source_quote: כִּי 'אַיֵּה' מְקוֹם כְּבוֹדוֹ – זֶה בְּחִינַת הַכָּבוֹד עֶלְיוֹן שֶׁל הַמַּאֲמָר הָעֶלְיוֹן

additions.reason: The sacrificial lamb of the olah ascent-offering, identified as the bechina of 'אַיֵּה' — the Akeidah verse 'וְאַיֵּה הַשֶּׂה לְעֹלָה' is read as: 'אַיֵּה' itself IS the she-la-olah.
additions.source_quote: שֶׁבְּחִינַת 'אַיֵּה' הִיא בְּחִינוֹת שֶׂה לְעוֹלָה, לְתַקֵּן וּלְכַפֵּר הִרְהוּר הַלֵּב

additions.reason: The 'vacant space' that appears devoid of divinity, yet secretly receives its life-force from the maamar satum. Neutral because it is a structural concept (the space of apparent absence) that is ultimately sustained by the hidden glory.
additions.source_quote: זֶה סוֹד בְּחִינַת חָלָל הַפָּנוּי, שֶׁהוּא כִּבְיָכוֹל פָּנוּי מֵאֱלֹקוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ ... אַךְ זֶהוּ בְּחִינָה הַנַּ"ל, שֶׁמְּקַבֵּל חִיּוּת מִבְּחִינַת מַאֲמָר סָתוּם

additions.reason: Divine glory as the root and purpose of all creation. The Torah opens with: 'כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה הוּא הַכָּבוֹד'. This is the dominant concept of Package 2.
additions.source_quote: כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה הוּא הַכָּבוֹד. כִּי כָל מַה שֶּׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לֹא בְּרָאוֹ אֶלָּא לִכְבוֹדוֹ

additions.reason: The ten utterances of creation, each containing its own specific kavod as its root. The structure through which divine glory is distributed and bounded in creation.
additions.source_quote: בְּכָל מַאֲמָר וּמַאֲמָר יֵשׁ בּוֹ בְּחִינַת כָּבוֹד מְיֻחָד, שֶׁהוּא שָׁרְשׁוֹ, כִּי הַכָּבוֹד הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ הַכֹּל

additions.reason: The root of all creation, explicitly identified as kavod. A bechina-equivalent of kavod from the opening statement of the Torah.
additions.source_quote: נִמְצָא שֶׁכְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה

additions.reason: Simplicity and straightforwardness — the human orientation that aligns with divine kavod rather than one's own kavod. The Rebbe presents this as the essence of Yiddishkeit and the direct path to not stumbling. Placed in Package 2 (kavod domain) because temimut is the correct human response to kavod — it means acting only when there is kevod Hashem.
additions.source_quote: וְעִקָּר הַיַּהֲדוּת הוּא רַק לֵילֵךְ בִּתְמִימוּת וּבִפְשִׁיטוּת, בְּלִי שׁוּם חָכְמוֹת ... וְלִבְלִי לְהַשְׁגִּיחַ כְּלָל עַל כְּבוֹד עַצְמוֹ. רַק אִם יֵשׁ בָּזֶה כְּבוֹד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יַעֲשֶׂה

additions.reason: The mixed kelipah (shell) that twists the heart in circles and generates doubts. Explicitly named as bechina in line 14. The dominant concept of Package 3.
additions.source_quote: כִּי יֵשׁ קְלִפָּה, שֶׁהִיא מְעַקֶּמֶת וּמְסַבֶּבֶת הַלֵּב בְּעִקּוּמִים וְסִבּוּבִים וּבִלְבּוּלִים הַרְבֵּה, וְהִיא בְּחִינַת קְלִפַּת נֹגַהּ

additions.reason: The Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, identified as the bechina of the doubts/confusions that precede Torah insight. Equals klipat nogah.
additions.source_quote: וְאֵלּוּ הַסְּפֵקוֹת הֵם בְּחִינַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת נֹגַהּ

additions.reason: Doubts and troubling thoughts/contemplations — the experiential manifestation of klipat nogah. These are what the person falls into, and what the olah sacrifice atones for.
additions.source_quote: שֶׁנּוֹפֵל לִסְפֵקוֹת וְהִרְהוּרִים, וּמְהַרְהֵר אַחַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

additions.reason: The spinning/circular confusion of the heart — the biblical phrase (Psalms 38) explicitly identified as the bechina of klipat nogah in line 14.
additions.source_quote: לִבִּי סְחַרְחַר, כִּי יֵשׁ קְלִפָּה, שֶׁהִיא מְעַקֶּמֶת וּמְסַבֶּבֶת הַלֵּב ... וְהִיא בְּחִינַת קְלִפַּת נֹגַהּ

additions.reason: The polluted/defiled places — the spiritual-existential location of the fallen state dominated by klipat nogah. Used throughout the Torah to describe the fallen condition.
additions.source_quote: כְּשֶׁאָדָם נוֹפֵל, חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, לִבְחִינַת מְקוֹמוֹת אֵלּוּ, דְּהַיְנוּ לִבְחִינַת מְקוֹמוֹת הַמְטֻנָּפִים, וְנוֹפֵל לִסְפֵקוֹת וְהִרְהוּרִים

additions.reason: Return/repentance — explicitly called the bechina of seeking 'אַיֵּה מְקוֹם כְּבוֹדוֹ'. The essential act of return is expressed through the longing and searching for God's kavod.
additions.source_quote: וְזֶה בְּחִינוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה, כִּי זֶה עִקָּר הַתְּשׁוּבָה, כְּשֶׁאָדָם מְבַקֵּשׁ וּמְחַפֵּשׂ אַחַר כְּבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ

additions.reason: The ascent-offering (olah), which atones for the hirhurim/doubts of the heart. Identified in line 13 as the bechina of the upward movement from the fallen state.
additions.source_quote: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת קָרְבָּן עוֹלָה, שֶׁמְּכַפֵּר עַל הִרְהוּר הַלֵּב

additions.reason: The Tree of Life — the state reached when one passes through the doubts (eitz hada'at) and arrives at the Torah itself. The polar opposite of eitz hada'at tov vera.
additions.source_quote: וּכְשֶׁמַּגִּיעַ אֶל הַתּוֹרָה בְּעַצְמָהּ, זֶה בְּחִינַת עֵץ הַחַיִּים

additions.reason: The paradox concept: the descent is the ultimate ascent. The fall into doubts and polluted places, when it leads to the cry of 'אַיֵּה', IS itself the mechanism of the highest ascent. This is the Torah's central paradox.

explicit_bechina_statements_found.statement: 'אַיֵּה' מְקוֹם כְּבוֹדוֹ = כָּבוֹד עֶלְיוֹן = מַאֲמָר סָתוּם בְּרֵאשִׁית
'כִּי אַיֵּה הוּא בְּחִינוֹת מַאֲמָר סָתוּם' — confirmed again
לִבִּי סְחַרְחַר = קְלִפַּת נֹגַהּ = וְנֹגַהּ לוֹ סָבִיב
סְפֵקוֹת = עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע = נֹגַהּ
קָרְבָּן עוֹלָה מְכַפֵּר עַל הִרְהוּר הַלֵּב
עֵץ הַחַיִּים = הַגָּעָה אֶל הַתּוֹרָה בְּעַצְמָהּ (after passing through the doubts)

analysis_notes.additional_thematic_note: The Torah's structure has two parallel arguments running simultaneously: (A) The metaphysics of kavod: creation's root is kavod → each utterance has its own kavod → even fallen places receive life from the hidden kavod of maamar satum. (B) The spiritual psychology: one should walk in temimut → when one falls to doubts, the fall itself becomes the ascent → by crying 'where is His glory?' one reconnects to the hidden kavod. Both arguments converge on the same point: the hidden 'ayeh' = maamar satum is the answer to both the cosmic question (how do fallen places receive life?) and the personal question (how does one rise from the fall?).
